en_US.title: Public Archive Source Voice Label
en_US.website_article:
A source voice label is the small line that keeps an archive sentence honest. It names whether the sentence came from a Deep Reach office filing, a terminal receipt body, an object mark, a scanner read, a public-safe summary, or a Marauder field note. The label does not decide truth. It tells the reader whose truth-claim is being tested.

Without the label, a contradiction turns into fog. With the label, the archive can say that an office line claims one route while the object mark preserves another. The player can then follow proof order instead of treating the cleanest public sentence as final canon.
en_US.wiki_article: Source voice label: a provenance field that names the speaker lane behind an evidence sentence. Valid lanes include office filing, terminal receipt body, object mark, scanner read, public-safe summary, claimant-safe line, and Marauder annotation. The label is not a verdict and must not reveal final receiver, protected claimant, Atlas consequence, or legal result.
en_US.pda_codex: PDA voice label: read who is speaking before you trust the line. Office filing, object mark, scanner read, receipt body, public summary, and Marauder note carry different proof weight. If two voices disagree, keep both and follow the next-proof target.
en_US.scanner_entry: Scanner tag: source voice unresolved. Compare voice lane, affected field, confidence state, and proof order before accepting the cleaner line.
en_US.terminal_note: Terminal provenance note: this sentence is not anonymous archive truth. It carries a source voice. Preserve the voice label until the next proof target confirms or downgrades it.
en_US.evidence_caption: Source voice label preserved: office, object, scanner, public summary, and Marauder note must not collapse into one neutral sentence.
en_US.spoiler_policy: Safe to expose source voice type and affected field. Hold final receiver, protected claimant, final route branch, Atlas consequence, legal verdict, and rescue conclusion behind later proof gates.

en_US.title: Wiki Evidence Confidence Ladder
en_US.website_article:
The confidence ladder exists because HECTON-8 evidence fails in different ways. A scanner can be confident about material and weak about route. A terminal receipt can preserve the useful body while lying in the header. A public-safe summary can protect a person while cleaning an office. One flat trust score would hide the problem the player needs to solve.

The ladder names useful states instead: provisional, object-supported, receipt-body-supported, downgraded, held, contradicted, and resolved by later proof. These states are safe to show early because they explain how to read evidence without revealing who finally received the packet or what the final consequence becomes.
en_US.wiki_article: Evidence confidence ladder: a spoiler-safe set of confidence states for public and PDA evidence. The ladder can show provisional, object-supported, receipt-body-supported, scanner-downgraded, claimant-held, contradiction-open, and later-proof-resolved states. It must not replace proof order or expose final outcomes.
en_US.pda_codex: PDA confidence panel: do not treat confidence as one meter. Read the source voice, then the confidence state. Object support, receipt-body support, scanner downgrade, claimant hold, and contradiction-open states point to different next-proof targets.
en_US.scanner_entry: Scanner confidence tag: confidence applies to a field, not the whole story. Material, route, receiver, custody, and claimant fields can disagree.
en_US.terminal_note: Terminal confidence note: receipt body support can outrank a clean header. Keep confidence tied to the field that was actually observed.
en_US.evidence_caption: Confidence ladder active: trust the field state, not the cleanest public sentence.
en_US.spoiler_policy: Safe to show confidence state names and next-proof class. Hold final receiver, protected claimant, final route branch, Atlas consequence, legal verdict, and rescue conclusion behind later proof gates.

en_US.title: PDA Proof Escalation Warning
en_US.website_article:
A proof escalation warning appears when the next correct question would answer too much. It can happen when a contradiction card points toward a protected claimant, when a route alias starts revealing the final route branch, when a receipt chain approaches the final receiver, or when an Atlas-linked consequence would turn an early clue into an ending dossier.

The warning is not a dead end. It tells the reader which safe comparison remains available: source voice, affected field, scanner confidence, object mark, receipt body, or custody route. The archive keeps the player moving without printing the answer before the route has earned it.
en_US.wiki_article: Proof escalation warning: a PDA or archive caution state used when a valid next-proof target would cross a protected-identity, final-route, final-receiver, Atlas-consequence, or ending boundary. The warning should name the held proof class and one safe comparison still available.
